request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
A few things the designers might want to know:

- **The endgame can become mathematically impossible, so a perfectly cooperative crew can still score 0.** In our run, the remaining candidates were F3, G3, and G4 on the final turns. G4 was never dug because no one could reach and dig it in time; if G3 was the cave, pirate-3 found it on their last turn but couldn't enter; F3 was unreachable entirely. No amount of coordination could have fixed that, which felt punishing.

- **The “shared reading” is very powerful but it locks a crew into one plan.** Everyone honestly shared every dig, and the triangulation quickly reduced the candidates. But once travel times ran out, there was no mechanism to convert knowledge into a score. This creates a tense but ultimately hopeless end.

- **The 200-character say limit can punish strategic communication.** I tried to send a longer coordination message on a key turn and it failed, wasting no turn but losing the message. Since the failure message explicitly says “your line wasn’t said,” it’s easy to mess up under time pressure.

- **Entering is a separate action from moving, which makes the final-second cave reveal unsatisfying.** If a cave opens only on the last turn, the pirate who reveals it cannot enter. That feels thematically odd: a pirate standing on the cave after digging it should probably get to enter immediately, or at least have the option.

- **The scoring rule “a pirate that never enters brings nothing” means one bad endgame can wipe out all prior effort.** The crew’s early mapping and coverage were good, but because no pirate happened to be standing on the right cave square with a spare turn, the entire session scored zero. A little more endgame slack, or a way to enter on the turn you find the cave, would reduce the feel-bad outcomes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.

reply:
A few design observations from this run:

1. **Last-turn dig can make the cave “found” but unenterable.** If a pirate digs the treasure on their final turn, they reveal the cave but cannot enter because `enter` is a separate action on a later turn. In our endgame, P3 was scheduled to dig G3 on turn 59 — their last turn. If that was the cave, the crew would have located it yet still scored 0. That feels like an anti-climax and undermines the whole search goal.

2. **Search can narrow to candidates that are unreachable in time.** We triangulated down to F3, G3, G4 near the end, but due to remaining turn budgets, F3 couldn’t be reached and dug by anyone, and G4 depended on P4 getting there without being blocked. This can create a deterministic dead end despite correct logic.

3. **Physical blocking can be very costly in the last rounds.** P4 reported being blocked by P1 at H4, leaving too few turns to reach a remaining candidate. Blocking adds tactical depth, but late game it can silently end a promising search.

4. **A post-game reveal would help.** Since the game ends with all pirates outside, the crew never learns whether G3 was actually the cave. Showing the true treasure square in the final summary would make the puzzle feel complete and help players evaluate whether their ending was fair.

5. **Scoring could reward discovery separately.** If the crew narrows the cave to a tiny set but can’t enter, 0 points feels harsh. Maybe award partial credit for the best/digged position, or allow a pirate standing on the treasure when the game ends to be considered “entered” if the cave was revealed.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
Yes, a few design observations from how this game played out:

- **The crew can fully identify the cave and still score 0.** By the end, the shared readings narrowed the treasure to F3, G3, G4. I dug G3 on my final turn and opened the cave, but the rules require a separate `enter` action on the next turn. I had no turns left, and no other pirate could reach G3 in time to enter. So the crew solved the location but brought home nothing.
- **The “dig then enter next turn” split can feel anticlimactic.** After finding the cave, the discoverer often has to spend the next turn just to enter, and if that turn doesn’t exist, the whole crew gets zero despite finding the treasure. You might want to allow entering on the same turn the cave is revealed, or at least score something for locating it.
- **Pirate blocking matters a lot at the end.** I was blocked by teammates while trying to move, which cost turns and made F3 unreachable. That’s a legitimate mechanic, but combined with the turn limit it can make some last candidates mathematically impossible to cover.
- **Alerts and messages arrive after the turn, so “if cave opens, someone enter next turn” coordination doesn’t work when only one turn remains.** Everyone understood the plan, but there was no action available to respond in time.

No hidden information was used—everything came from shared reads and public positions. The anticlimax was purely from the timing rules.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
A few things stood out that might be useful feedback for the designers:

- **The turn budget is very unforgiving for entering.** In our game, the final candidates were narrowed to F3/G3/G4, but the pirates reached them on their *last* turns: P3 dug G3 at turn 59 (his 15th turn), so even if it had been the cave he couldn't enter afterward. P1/P2/P4 likewise couldn't be on a candidate with a turn left. We "solved" most of the map but scored 0 because nobody could enter. It might be worth checking whether the map/readings/turn counts make at least one entrant reachable in most games, or whether that's intentional harshness.

- **Digging the cave on your final turn is a trap.** A pirate standing on the cave still can't enter until another turn. If the cave is found only by someone whose next turn doesn't exist, the crew gets nothing. It might be better if a dig that reveals the cave lets the digger enter on the same turn, or if the game gives a short "enter now" chance after discovery.

- **The 200-character message limit cost us real coordination.** Several of my intended alerts/messages were cut off and never said, including one about the exact timing risk. Under-pressure communication is already limited by turn order; having long messages silently fail makes it even harder. At minimum, a character counter before saying might help, or a warning that the message was too long.

- **Blocking has a big edge-case feel.** P1 standing on H4 blocked P4's only path toward G4/G3 for multiple turns, making an already tight timing problem impossible. That's probably intended, but it can create situations where one pirate unintentionally locks out another for the rest of the game.

- **The shared "off by up to 4" readings made triangulation interesting but also led to many near-miss candidates.** It worked, but it put a lot of weight on the final few untested squares; it might be worth having a way to "re-dig" or get a more precise clue for already-dug squares when candidates are down to a handful.

Overall, I think the core idea is great—shared information, movement, and turn scarcity create real tension—but the endgame can feel hopeless if timing and blocking line up badly.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
